title: Streamlined contract redline decision path and sales preflight
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Sales engineers and AEs spend 40–60% of contract negotiation time on basic redline triage (indemnity caps, data residency clauses, liability language) which slows deal velocity and causes inconsistent pricing concessions. Goal: Build a lightweight decision path + sales preflight tool that automates initial redline scoring, surfaces recommended concession bands, and wires approvals into pricing experiments so we can safely fast-track low-risk deals and surface high-risk deals to Legal/Revenue Ops. Scope: MSA/DPA redline scoring model, DPA-specific clause mapping, concession band suggestions (indemnity/liability tiers), UI microflow embedded in the CRM pre-sign checklist, integration with pricing engine for quick quotes, playbook composer for AE talking points, and telemetry to measure cycle time and accuracy. Out of scope for MVP: fully automated countersignature, on-prem contract authoring templates. Success metrics: reduce average legal turnaround from 7 to 2 business days for low-risk redlines, increase win rate on enterprise pilot accounts by 6%, reduce AE time spent on triage by 30% in pilot. Acceptance criteria: (1) Redline auto-score model delivers >=85% precision on low vs high risk classification for historical dataset; (2) UI preflight returns a recommended concession band and suggested clause text for the AE and records a decision; (3) Pricing engine accepts preflight output and produces a draft quote; (4) Legal queue receives enriched context (clause extract, score, suggested fallback) and SLA routing works for canary customers. Compliance: ensure flagged PII clauses go through security_review_required and KMS/SSO controls are retained. Rollout strategy: pilot with two field pods (mid-market and enterprise AE teams) for 4 weeks, gather feedback, then open to all US sales; Dedicated/Private customers will see a guarded checkbox and redline telemetry will be masked for customers with strict NDAs.
